title: Phononic Frequency Combs in Twisted Bilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Heterostructures from First Principles
abstract: Phononic frequency combs are equidistant spectral ladders generated when a driven vibrational mode transfers energy to an autoparametrically excited subharmonic mode through anharmonic intermode coupling. In previous studies, the coupling strength governing this energy transfer has typically been treated as a free parameter, extracted from a fabricated device, or adopted from an earlier calculation for a specific mode pair. As a result, whether a given crystal can support a phononic frequency comb, and the drive strength required to generate it, has not been predictable a priori. Here we obtain the complete parameter set from density functional theory. Twisted bilayers of \MoSSe{} and \MoSMoSe{} at the commensurate angle $21.787^{\circ}$ adopt space group $P3$ in a 42-atom \rootseven{} moiré supercell. The second-order force constants provide the mode frequencies; the third-order constants provide the linewidths through the Boltzmann transport equation and hence the quality factors; and the same third-order tensor projected onto the phonon eigenvectors of a chosen mode pair provides the anharmonic couplings $\kt$ and $\kss$. Both bilayers constitute a mode pair within $0.8\%$ of the $2\!:\!1$ resonance with $ω_1/ω_2 = 1.9923$ in \MoSSe{} and $1.9943$ in \MoSMoSe{}. By integrating the resulting two-mode equations, both modes generate combs through a discontinuous transition: at $701\,\fth$ in \MoSSe{} the envelope variance rises from $2.1\times10^{3}$ to $1.37\times10^{4}$ and the tooth count of mode 1 from 7 to 16 within a single $5\,\fth$ increment, identifying the onset as subcritical. The spectral entropy peaks \emph{before} this jump, at $341\,\fth$. The two compounds carry comparable coupling, differing by a factor of $1.2$. However, the comb excitation threshold is set by the quality-factors of signal modes: $Q_2 = 672$ for \MoSSe{} and $Q_2 = 3844$ for \MoSMoSe{}.
summary: This work uses first-principles DFT calculations to model phononic frequency combs in twisted TMD heterostructures. By calculating the full anharmonic coupling parameters, the authors predict the precise conditions—including the drive strength threshold—under which these spectral combs form. This provides a powerful, predictive tool for designing novel quantum materials based on lattice dynamics.
main_problem: To predict a priori whether a given crystal can support a phononic frequency comb and to determine the required drive strength, overcoming previous limitations where coupling strengths were treated as free parameters.
main_result: The study successfully predicts comb generation in twisted TMD heterostructures, showing that the comb excitation threshold is set by the quality factors of the signal modes, and that the comb behavior is strongly chemistry dependent.
method: The authors used Density Functional Theory (DFT) to calculate the complete parameter set, including second- and third-order force constants, which were then used to solve coupled, non-linear two-mode differential equations.
model_or_system: The system is a twisted bilayer heterostructure of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides (TMDs), specifically MoS2/WSe2 and MoS2/MoSe2, forming a moiré supercell. The physics is modeled by the energy transfer between two coupled vibrational modes exhibiting an approximate 2:1 internal resonance.
key_observables: Comb tooth count, envelope variance, spectral entropy, and the comb excitation threshold (f_th).
important_parameters: The resonance ratio (omega_1/omega_2 ≈ 1.99), the quality factors (Q_2), and the anharmonic coupling constants (kappa_12, kappa_22).
main_assumptions: The analysis is limited to a two-mode reduction, and the calculation of linewidths relies on random displacement sampling for third-order force constants, which is noted as a potential source of systematic error.
figures_summary: The notes mention Figure 4 showing spectral entropy and envelope variance versus drive for both heterostructures, and Table II quantitatively comparing comb characteristics between the two compounds.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem (predicting comb existence), details the first-principles methodology (DFT for force constants), presents the theoretical model (two-mode coupled equations), and concludes by comparing the results for the two different TMD bilayers.
why_interesting: The study models non-linear energy transfer in lattice vibrations, which is a key concept in open quantum systems and nonlinear dynamics. The use of first-principles methods to derive coupling parameters is highly relevant for designing quantum materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 2. Phononic frequency combs in the two heterostructures at the same drive, f0 = 1186 fth. (a) MoS2/WSe2; (b) MoS2/MoSe2. In each, upper panels show the time-domain displacement of the driven mode (blue) and of the parametrically excited mode (orange); lower panels show the corresponding spectra about ω1 and ω2, with the mode frequencies marked by dashed lines. The envelope modulation in the time domain is the beating of the comb teeth against one another.

FIG. 3. Drive sweeps of the two heterostructures, with drive in units of fth for each compound. (a) MoS2/WSe2; (b) MoS2/MoSe2. In each, from top: root-mean-square amplitude of the parametrically excited mode (X2), comb tooth count in mode 1 and in mode 2, and root-mean-square amplitude of the driven mode (X1). The dashed line marks comb onset and the dotted line comb death, which is not reached within the MoS2/MoSe2 sweep. All quantities change discontinuously at onset, identifying it as a subcritical transition.

FIG. 4. Spectral entropy (upper trace of each panel) and envelope variance of the driven mode (lower trace) against drive. (a) MoS2/WSe2; (b) MoS2/MoSe2. Shaded bands mark the detected regimes; the dash-dotted line marks the entropy maximum, the dashed line comb onset and the dotted line comb death (MoS2/WSe2 only). In both compounds the entropy maximum precedes the onset, at which the entropy falls and the variance jumps to its plateau.
